text:
amal: Heads-up: telemetry flagged an ephemeral-keystore leaking wrapped ciphertexts in partner ingest logs. pattern across 3 runs, small sample below. not yet public but high priority.

amal: ```
INFO 2025-07-12T03:11:02Z ingest: received blob id=blk_7f2a wrap_ciphertext=CiQ...
INFO 2025-07-12T03:11:05Z ingest: received blob id=blk_7f2b wrap_ciphertext=CiQ...
```

jonah: I see. Looks like the job mounted a local keystore dir that should have been excluded. Which KMS key was used to wrap?

linh: Key is projects/redwood-prod/locations/global/keyRings/ingest/cryptoKeys/keystore-wrap-v2 (v3). Partner SA had ENCRYPT/DECRYPT grants for a short-lived onboarding window.

security-bot: ALERT: partner-ingest@partner-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com used keystore-wrap-v2 at 2025-07-12T03:12:01Z (wrap).

maria: Proposed immediate actions: 1) revoke partner SA encrypt/wrap grants 2) create ephemeral wrap key and rewrap affected ciphertexts 3) rotate consumer credentials and CI tokens 4) apply RBAC change to prevent keystore mounts in ingest jobs 5) bump Vault audit retention + add alert for abnormal wrap rate.

jonah: For rewrap: we need a safe migration path so consumers can still decrypt old blobs during cutover. Plan: dual-wrap support in the ingest path for ~24h: try new key, fallback to old. Then run bulk rewrap to new key. I'll own the script.

maria: That sounds right. We should also snapshot which blobs touched partner SA, export list to a GCS object (access-controlled) and run rewrap in small batches.

linh: I'll revoke the grant now and push an RBAC change to remove ENCRYPT/WRAP from partner SA and keep only DECRYPT if needed. applying terraform snippet: 

linh: ```hcl
resource "google_kms_crypto_key_iam_binding" "ingest_partner_restrict" {
  crypto_key_id = "${var.ingest_key}"
  role = "roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter"
  members = ["serviceAccount:partner-ingest@partner-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com"]
}
# later replace with a more restrictive custom role removing encrypt where appropriate
```

jonah: Rewrap command I'll run (dry-run first):

jonah: ```bash
gcloud kms keys versions add-iam-policy-binding --key=keystore-wrap-v3 --member="serviceAccount:rewrap-runner@redwood-infra.iam.gserviceaccount.com" --role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter
python tools/rewrap_keystore.py --src-key projects/redwood-prod/.../keystore-wrap-v2 --dst-key projects/redwood-prod/.../keystore-wrap-v3 --batch-size 200 --dry-run
```

sre-oncall: I'm oncall and will coordinate a short deploy freeze for ingest. ETA 45-60m to revoke grants, run dry-run in staging, then run small prod batch. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

amal: Also: bump Vault audit log retention for the ingest namespace to 90d and add an alert rule: wrap_calls_from_same_sa > 3/min => pager. @linh can you add that to audit rules?

linh: Yep. Adding a transient alert and increasing retention. Will post PR link shortly.

maria: After rewrap completes we'll rotate long-lived secrets: partner app tokens, any AKS secrets that referenced the old ciphertext, and CI runner keys. Add runbook step: revoke old wrap key versions after 72h and confirm no decryption errors.

security-bot: Ticket created: SEC-2178 - "ephemeral keystore exposure: rewrap + RBAC lockdown". Assignees: jonah, linh, amal, maria. Priority: P1.

amal: Good work team. Once the revocation + rewrap runs, capture a short post-run checklist and we'll add a postmortem with remediation items (policy to block keystore mounts, RBAC gating, audit alerts). Follow-up in this thread in 24h.
